However, none of the cited evidence (E2, E3, E4) provides data or discussion linking this oxide film to reduced wear via a mechanical barrier mechanism, nor do they compare wear performance of oxidized vs. non-oxidized coatings. E3 only speculates on protective characteristics of Fe2O3 and spinel phases for SOFC interconnects, not wear. The mechanistic premises about wear reduction are unsupported by the cited passag
premises: Thermal exposure at 800°C forms a continuous, adherent (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 spinel oxide film on the equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu HEA coating.
This spinel oxide film acts as a mechanical barrier that reduces direct asperity contact and plastic deformation during sliding wear.
The uniform equiatomic composition ensures the continuity of the oxide film.
The formation of this oxide film is thermally activated and governs enhanced wear performance.
The oxide film reduces wear rates and friction coefficients compared to as-deposited coatings without controlled oxidation.
